text:
maria: Noticed a latency tail after yesterday's kernel handoff in the continuous batcher.  p50 okay, p95 up ~120ms. Anyone else seeing this?
chris: saw it on the canary graphs, looks like batch formation time increased.
maria: interesting — kernel selection changed to the new matmul path at 3 tokens for that model. Could that be increasing microbatch churn?
kai: possible. new kernel has higher per-call overhead but better throughput at larger seqs. For small microbatches it can lose.
prashant: can you paste the perf trace?
maria: sure, here's a slice from the request profiler:
```
TS  RPC recv  queue_ms  batch_ms  kernel_select_ms  kernel_exec_ms
12:02:01  2ms   18ms    14ms       6ms               32ms
12:02:02  1ms   42ms    22ms       9ms               28ms
12:02:03  3ms   10ms     9ms       5ms               33ms
```
maria: batch_ms ticked up, queue_ms also has more variance.
emily: do we have KV-hit breakdown? maybe cache miss patterns are causing shorter effective sequences -> more small batches.
chris: KV hit rate actually dropped ~6% on that window. Could be eviction churn from the new batching timing.
kai: hypothesis: kernel selection threshold combined with slightly later batch cut increases inter-request spacing, which lowers KV coalescing.
prashant: sounds like a feedback loop: kernel switch -> more small batches -> worse KV locality -> longer tails -> more small batches.
maria: agreed. Two quick experiments: 1) force old kernel for seq<=8 for 24h on canary, 2) tweak batch-formation hold window from 6ms -> 3ms. Which do we prefer to run first?
emily: run both in parallel on different canary shards if possible. compare p95 + kv-hit.
chris: I can spin up an A/B for 6h each. I'll use these knobs:
```
# admit config
batching.hold_ms = 6 -> 3
kernel.selector.small_seq_threshold = 3 -> 8 (force old)
```
prashant: add metric to track "preempted_batches" and "kv_recombo" so we can correlate.
perf-bot: deployed metric probe perf.metrics.preempted_batches to canary-2 at 12:28 UTC
kai: also consider soft-admit tweak: increase token_budget_target by 10% to allow slightly larger batches under light load. Should reduce microbatching.
emily: careful, that changes latency/cost tradeoff. But for canary it's fine.
maria: ok plan: chris runs A/B with two shards (kernel-force vs hold-window) + token_budget bump on a 3rd shard. 6h run. collect p50/p95, kv-hit, preempted_batches.
chris: starting now. will post interim graphs.
(prashant reacts with :thumbsup:)
chris: 12:36 update — kernel-force shard p95 improved ~80ms, kv-hit back to baseline. hold-window shard shows p95 improved ~40ms but kv-hit only slight improvement. token_budget bump lowered preempt rates but p50 latency rose ~10ms.
prashant: that suggests kernel path was the main amplifier.
maria: sounds like long-term fix is smarter selector + a short hysteresis to avoid flipping on transient seq changes. maybe require >N consecutive requests before picking new kernel for a model shard.
kai: agree. add a min-dwell of 30s and require avg_seq delta > 2 tokens to switch. also track impact on KV hit.
emily: I'll draft the selector change and a canary rollout plan. include rollback to previous kernel mapping and flag for dynamic token_budget.
chris: logging note: emit `kernel_switch_reason` with context so we can debug future regressions.
maria: thanks. action items: emily drafts PR for selector + hysteresis, chris will run a wider canary with min-dwell, prashant will add the recombo metrics, kai will write a short doc on kernel tradeoffs for runtime. I'll summarize in the eng-runtime sync.
perf-bot: canary audit event created: audit/1785 (maria)
maria: thanks all, closing the thread once PRs land.
